1|# COUPLE BIBLE — CANON (Day 1)
2|
3|## WHO THEY ARE
4|
5|**Elias Ward**, 35. Runs "Ward & Son," a two-van heating-and-plumbing crew. There is no son and never was — his father Tom started the company; Tom died three years ago and Elias kept the name because repainting both vans felt like losing him twice. Left school at 17 to work under his dad. Hands always smell faintly of flux and solder. Married 4 years (anniversary: 12 September), together 8. Lives in a 1930s semi on Ferndale Road.
6|
7|**Maren Ward**, 33 (née Kowalczyk — she kept her name professionally; his mother "forgets" it constantly). Charge nurse, paediatric ward at St Aldhelm's, rotating day/night shifts. Daughter of Polish immigrants; grew up translating hospital letters for her mother. Organised to the point of ritual: labelled jars, a shared calendar nobody else maintains, a notebook of "things Elias almost said."
8|
9|## QUIRKS
10|
11|- Elias: fixes things around the house *instead of* talking — she'll wake to a silenced door hinge mid-argument. Writes reminders on the back of his hand. Calls her "Mare" and nothing else.
12|- Maren: narrates traffic when driving ("indicator, love, it's free"). Sings specific songs badly when anxious — ABBA's "Slipping Through My Fingers," always that one. Keeps the notebook; page one is dated their wedding day.
13|
14|## THE THING EACH NEVER SAYS ALOUD
15|
16|- **Elias:** that he's terrified he'll be bad at marriage the way his dad was bad at it — Tom provided brilliantly and vanished emotionally — and that every silent fixed hinge is him begging without having to.
17|- **Maren:** that she's started keeping score — that his family takes and hers thanks — and that she's frightened the marriage is becoming logistics: two calendars negotiating custody of a weekend.
18|
19|## THE THREE LIVE TENSIONS
20|
21|1. **MONEY — the £9,400.** Six weeks ago Elias moved £9,400 out of the joint "Ferndale Fund" (house-deposit savings, 3 years of skimming) to cover his brother Callum's defaulted van-lease. Told her nothing. She found it on a paper statement Tuesday. His position: it's my brother, it's my money too, problem solved. Hers: the amount is survivable; the secrecy is not. Last night ended: her — "I'm not angry about the money." Him — "Then what?" Neither answered. She slept facing the wall.
22|
23|2. **FAMILY — two mothers, one compass.** Maren's mother **Beata** (61, early Parkinson's, 90 minutes away in Leeds) asked gently last week whether they'd ever consider moving closer — Maren wants to say yes and hasn't dared. Elias's mother **Pat** (66, ten minutes away, Sunday roast is law) treats Maren's nursing as "a phase she'll grow out of" and the surname as a personal insult. Each spouse privately believes the other's family always wins.
24|
25|3. **TIME — four dinners.** His crew takes emergency call-outs nights and weekends; she rotates shifts. Maren counted: four dinners together last month, one without phones. The shared calendar she built has become a battlefield — he double-books it, then apologises with flowers, which she has started putting in the boot-room vase without comment.
26|
27|## STATE GOING INTO DAY 1
28|
29|It's Thursday. Tonight's 7pm dinner at Trattoria Verde — booked two weeks ago, the "proper talk" Maren demanded — collides with a £400 emergency boiler call-out Elias took at 4:40pm because the Ferndale Fund hole suddenly makes money real. Pat has invited herself and Callum to Sunday roast. Beata's specialist appointment landed Tuesday 10:40 in Leeds and needs a driver. Everything above is canon; nothing else has happened yet.

1|# DAY 1 — THURSDAY (weave)
2|
3|*Sources: couple_bible.md (canon), boy/boy_in.md + boy/answer.md (Elias), girl/girl_in.md + girl/answer.md (Maren). All dialogue below is quoted verbatim from the answer files. No prior day files exist; this is Day 1.*
4|
5|---
6|
7|## Scene 1 — 4:52pm, Van 2, Ashgrove Lane
8|
9|The job sheet says EMERGENCY — NO HOT WATER. £400, tonight only. Six weeks ago £400 was rounding error; since he emptied the Ferndale Fund, it's rent-money [bible §Tension 1; boy/answer.md]. Elias takes the call-out — Mrs. Whoever is cold either way — but first, this time, his thumb actually presses send:
10|
11|> "Emergency call-out. Boiler dead, old lady, no hot water. I'll be late — 7:30, maybe 8. Don't order. I'm coming. Wear the green thing. — E"
12|
13|Then, before the boiler, the harder call. He rings his mother back and says the hard part *before* Sunday, not after:
14|
15|> "Mum — we'll be there. But you don't spring Callum on Mare at our table. You tell her yourself, and you tell her tonight."
16|
17|One untold thing killed. By his own count, two left [boy/answer.md] — and the biggest one, the one about Dad, isn't scheduled for tonight.
18|
19|## Scene 2 — 5:04pm, Ferndale Road, the bathroom
20|
21|Maren, twelve-hour shift behind her, a baby's cannula four attempts deep, is braiding wet hair when the phone buzzes on the shelf. She reads it twice. *Wear the green thing.* The dress was already ironed — for a restaurant, not for him [girl/girl_in.md]. She does not text back a heart. She does not text back at all. But she goes downstairs and puts the paper statement in her handbag — not to wave it around, just so it's *there* [girl/answer.md].
22|
23|In the car she catches herself humming it — ABBA, *Slipping Through My Fingers*, always that one [bible §Quirks] — and stops at the chorus, because even her anxiety has started keeping score.
24|
25|## Scene 3 — 7:00pm, Trattoria Verde, table for two
26|
27|She's seated at 7:00 exactly. Water ordered. Phone in bag, unread-dark. Across the room the 7:15 couple already aren't speaking; she watches them the way you watch a possible future. The statement sits in the handbag between the breadsticks and where he'll be [girl/answer.md].
28|
29|7:41pm. The door. Elias — smelling of gas sealant over the permanent flux-and-solder, a reminder inked on the back of his hand in his own handwriting: **THEN WHAT** [bible §Quirks; boy/answer.md]. He sits. He puts the phone face-down on the table before the menus arrive. Neither of them mentions the flowers he hasn't brought — for once there are no flowers, which is its own kind of message [bible §Tension 3].
30|
31|## Scene 4 — Before the mains
32|
33|He starts, because he promised himself he would, before the mains:
34|
35|> "Mum's bringing Callum Sunday. To celebrate us sorting things out — her words. I should've told you Tuesday. I'm telling you now."
36|
37|Maren sets down her fork. Opens the handbag. Lays the paper statement on the tablecloth — nine thousand, four hundred, highlighted in ward-shift yellow — and says the true thing [girl/answer.md]:
38|
39|> "I wasn't angry about the money, and I need to say the true thing now: you decided alone, and I found out from a piece of paper. Nine thousand, four hundred. Three years of us, six weeks of silence."
40|
41|He doesn't reach for the statement. He reaches for the question he owes her, the one inked on his hand:
42|
43|> "Last night I asked 'then what' and you turned to the wall. I'm asking again. Then what, Mare? Say it ugly if you have to. I'm not leaving the table till I've heard it."
44|
45|She says it ugly. Or rather, she says it worse than ugly — she says it fair [girl/answer.md]:
46|
47|> "And I noticed part of me had already forgiven you before I'd even said it out loud. That scared me more than the number did. I don't want to be someone who forgives by default. I want to be asked."
48|
49|For a man whose love language is a silenced door hinge, it lands like a diagnosis. *I want to be asked.* He writes it on the back of his hand, under the first line, while she watches.
50|
51|## Scene 5 — Before pudding
52|
53|Maren turns the page — her turn to ask [girl/answer.md]:
54|
55|> "Tuesday, 10:40. I'm taking Mum. Tell me if the rota fights me — but don't tell me no because Sunday belongs to Callum again."
56|
57|He answers before she's finished the sentence — yes. He doesn't know yet why it matters, and says that's exactly why he says it [boy/answer.md]. The shared calendar, that battlefield [bible §Tension 3], gets its first uncontested entry of the autumn: **Tue — Leeds, Mum, 10:40. HELD.**
58|
59|Puddles of tiramisu. Two spoons. Nobody checks a phone. First dinner without one since the count began [bible §Tension 3; girl/answer.md].
60|
61|## Scene 6 — How the day ended
62|
63|They close the place politely, at the waitress's third pass. In the car park they stand by Van 2 a moment longer than needed. He drives home late — but he drives home [boy/answer.md]. Maren, upstairs, opens the notebook — page one still dated their wedding day, *he looked at me like I was the answer* — and for the first time in weeks writes down something he actually said, instead of what he almost said [bible §Quirks; girl/answer.md].
64|
65|Lights out on Ferndale Road, 11:20pm. Nobody sleeps facing the wall.
66|
67|---
68|
69|## DECISIONS MADE (Day 1)
70|
71|1. **Elias took the £400 emergency call-out** — the fund hole made the money real; he chose both the job and the dinner, late. [boy/answer.md]
72|2. **Sunday roast stands — conditionally.** Elias told Pat she must personally tell Maren about Callum *tonight*, not spring it at the table. Whether Pat complied is **unconfirmed** — no call or text from Pat appears in either answer. (Open thread.) [boy/answer.md]
73|3. **The roast secret is dead.** Elias disclosed Sunday/Callum to Maren himself, at the table, before the mains — the third untold thing, told. [boy/answer.md]
74|4. **"Then what" was answered.** Maren named the real wound — *you decided alone, and I found out from a piece of paper* — and confessed the scarier half: she forgives by default and doesn't want to. New house standard, his handwriting: **ASK FIRST.** [girl/answer.md]
75|5. **Leeds, Tuesday 10:40 — locked.** Maren takes her mother; Elias's yes came before she finished the sentence. [both answers]
76|6. **The £9,400 itself: untouched.** The wound was named; the repayment/rebuild terms were **not** discussed in either answer. Deliberately left open. (NOT IN CONTEXT — flagged for Day 2.)
77|
78|## EMOTIONAL CARRY-OVER INTO TOMORROW (Friday)
79|
80|- **Elias** (fear 8 → easing; affection 6 and climbing; happiness 3, up one since "wear the green thing"): lighter by one secret, heavier by one promise. *Ask first* is written on his hand and will survive the shower; whether it survives Sunday is the real test. Two untold things remain by his own count — and the deepest one, the fear of being Tom, has never been said aloud to anyone [bible §Never-Says; boy/answer.md].
81|- **Maren** (happiness 2; fear 7 rising but spent; affection 6 — "that's the problem and the hope"): she said the true thing and wasn't punished for it. The notebook entry tonight is in a new tense. But she heard herself say *don't tell me no because Sunday belongs to Callum again* — the score-keeper is still keeping score, one dinner at a time [girl/answer.md].
82|- **Between them, unresolved for Day 2:** (a) Did Pat actually call Maren tonight, as instructed — and what tone did she use? (b) Sunday roast with Callum, framed as "celebration," now unavoidable. (c) The £9,400: rebuild the fund? Terms with Callum? Never discussed. (d) Tuesday's Leeds drive is the first calendar promise either of them has made that the other believes.
83|- **The week's trajectory:** Day 1 ended in repair — barely, honestly, with both of them choosing speech over hinges and flowers. The log builds from here; no resets.

1|# DAY 2 — FRIDAY (weave)
2|
3|*Sources: couple_bible.md (canon), boy/boy_in.md + boy/answer.md (Elias), girl/girl_in.md + girl/answer.md (Maren), day1.md (prior canon). All dialogue below is quoted verbatim from the answer files. Day 1's open threads — Pat's call, the £9,400 terms, Sunday — are all addressed; nothing reset.*
4|
5|---
6|
7|## Scene 1 — 6:50am, two kitchens (his: Ferndale Road; hers: St Aldhelm's staff room)
8|
9|Maren's out the door since 6:25 — a kiss half a second longer than yesterday's [boy/boy_in.md]. Elias eats toast standing up, Van 2 keys on the counter, and decides the ink on his hand is still wet enough to matter. Before the radiator job, before the van even warms up, two texts to Mare — not tonight, now [boy/answer.md]:
10|
11|> "Up. Two things before I forget them. 1) Callum texted 11:15 last night — 'sorted the van thing, bit tight this side of xmas.' No amount, no date. Haven't replied. You hear it from me, second time running. 2) The Ferndale Fund standing order — £250, fires Monday, and the fund's empty because I emptied it. I forgot it existed. What do we do — pause it, feed it, kill it? Your call as much as mine. — E"
12|
13|Twelve miles away, cold coffee, Maren answers her mother before the ward takes her [girl/answer.md]:
14|
15|> *"Elias is trying. Tuesday I'm driving Mum myself — Basia keeps her Saturday."*
16|
17|She still doesn't know how to answer Beata's *How is Elias?* — so she answers it sideways, with the truth she has: *trying* [girl/girl_in.md].
18|
19|## Scene 2 — 8:00am, the rota office and Mossley Rise
20|
21|Maren rings the rota coordinator at eight and declines the Saturday double-time. Her voice shakes saying it — the Ferndale Fund fires Monday regardless, and £250 is £250 — but last night cost her a true thing and paid back a sentence in a notebook, and she's not trading the first weekend of that for overtime [girl/answer.md].
22|
23|Same hour, Elias is bleeding a radiator at Mossley Rise when he rings her back on speaker — Sunday, the frost, the choice she doesn't know he's making [boy/answer.md]:
24|
25|> "Sunday. Frost means every boiler in town dies by nine — I could earn a week's takings. And I'd rather be at Mum's table watching Callum squirm. So: I work till noon, arrive late but arrive, and I tell Mum today that's the deal. Unless you'd rather I not come at all — say it, I'll take it."
26|
27|Then Callum gets his answer, terms attached, because Mare's had hers first [boy/answer.md]:
28|
29|> "Van thing's settled, ta. Money: send £200 by Christmas or say you can't — either's fine, silence isn't. And you'll be civil to Mare Sunday or stay home."
30|
31|## Scene 3 — Lunch break, the receipt returned
32|
33|Maren cancels the receipt in her head — the one she's been holding since yesterday, 6:05pm, Pat's voice saying *so it comes from me, dear* [girl/girl_in.md]. Self-defence, she's decided. Not score-keeping. She takes out her phone and texts him [girl/answer.md]:
34|
35|> *"Pat rang yesterday, 6:05. Before you told me. I already knew about Sunday and let you say it anyway. Coming home normal tonight. — M"*
36|
37|He gets to hear it from her before he hears it from Pat twice. The last withheld thing between them from Day 1 — the call nobody could confirm — is now on the table, from her side, voluntarily [day1.md §Open threads; girl/answer.md].
38|
39|## Scene 4 — Evening, shoes off, kettle on
40|
41|She says it out loud properly, because a text is a text and this deserves air [girl/answer.md]:
42|
43|> "I kept Pat's call back for one day and I hated how natural it felt. So — she rang. She does your agreeing for you, Elias, and I sat on it. That's mine to own. Ask first, remember? I'm asking: come to Sunday with me, or don't go."
44|
45|And on the standing order — the £9,400's first concrete terms, forty-eight hours late [girl/answer.md; day1.md §Decision 6]:
46|
47|> "The £250 can fire Monday. But we set the terms together or I turn it off. Your account, our fund — pick a number with me."
48|
49|He asked first twice this morning; she asks first now, owning the one thing she kept. The symmetry is not lost on either of them [bible §Tension 1; both answers].
50|
51|## Scene 5 — How the day ended
52|
53|The kettle boils. The standing order stays armed for Monday — the number unpicked, because picking it is Sunday-conversation, maybe better [girl/answer.md leaves the choice open]. On the back of his hand, ASK FIRST has survived its second shower [boy/boy_in.md]. In the notebook, under page one and under last night's entry, nothing new yet — today's pages live in texts and a kettle speech, and she writes slower now, like the words cost more [bible §Quirks; girl/answer.md].
54|
55|Two repair days in a row. Neither of them trusts it yet. Lights out on Ferndale Road with Sunday two days out and the first frost forecast to kill every boiler in town by nine [boy/boy_in.md].
56|
57|---
58|
59|## DECISIONS MADE (Day 2)
60|
61|1. **Elias disclosed Callum's text and the standing order unprompted, before 7am** — "you hear it from me, second time running." The decide-alone pattern, twice burned, formally broken. [boy/answer.md]
62|2. **Sunday plan set by Elias: work till noon, arrive late but arrive** — and he handed Maren the veto ("unless you'd rather I not come at all"). No veto recorded in her answer; the offer stands. He commits to telling Pat the deal today. [boy/answer.md]
63|3. **Callum issued terms: £200 by Christmas or say you can't — "silence isn't" — plus civility to Maren Sunday or stay home.** Callum's response: NOT IN CONTEXT, unanswered on the page. (Open thread.) [boy/answer.md]
64|4. **Maren declined the Saturday double-time** — the thin weekend beat £250. Voice shook; she did it anyway. [girl/answer.md]
65|5. **Maren disclosed Pat's 6:05pm call** — ruled self-defence, not score-keeping, and owned aloud in the evening: "that's mine to own." Day 1's unconfirmed thread (did Pat call?) resolved: she did, before Elias's dinner disclosure. [girl/girl_in.md + girl/answer.md; day1.md]
66|6. **Standing order: conditional truce.** The £250 may fire Monday, but only under jointly-set terms — "pick a number with me." The number itself: NOT YET CHOSEN. (Open thread — first item for Day 3.) [girl/answer.md]
67|7. **Beata thread advanced:** Tuesday driving confirmed by Maren personally; Basia keeps her Saturday; Beata's *How is Elias?* answered only as "trying." [girl/answer.md]
68|
69|## EMOTIONAL CARRY-OVER INTO TOMORROW (Saturday)
70|
71|- **Elias** (fear 6, down from 8; affection 7 and climbing; happiness 4; anger 3 — at Callum, not her; disgust 2, at himself for forgetting his own standing order; sadness 5, below the eleven-day floor of 6): the texts are sent and dread shrank when it was spoken [boy/answer.md]. Repair wins again, four seeds in five. One untold thing left by his own count — Dad — and it doesn't have a Sunday deadline. Yet [boy/boy_in.md].
72|- **Maren** (happiness 3, up one; fear 6 falling; affection 7 — "he didn't flinch"; loneliness 4, "twenty minutes and one honest text closer"; disgust 4, at how *natural* keeping the receipt felt): she sent the text before she could rehearse it, and the world held [girl/answer.md]. The score-keeper caught herself keeping score and put the book down — this time.
73|- **Between them, unresolved for Day 3:** (a) the number — the fund's rebuild terms, deferred to a conversation neither has scheduled; (b) Callum's reply to his ultimatum, and whether £200-by-Christmas holds; (c) Pat's reaction to "work till noon, arrive late" — Elias committed to telling her today, outcome unrecorded; (d) Sunday itself: Callum at the table, "celebration" framing intact, first frost stacking boilers against the clock; (e) the Dad conversation — the last untold thing, no deadline, approaching anyway; (f) Maren's answer to Beata's *How is Elias?* — "trying" was a down payment on a harder sentence.
74|- **The week's trajectory:** two repair days back to back — speech over hinges, receipts surrendered voluntarily, terms attached to silences. The log builds; the stress test is Sunday, and both of them know it. No resets.

1|# DAY 3 — SATURDAY (weave)
2|
3|*Sources: couple_bible.md (canon), boy/boy_in.md + boy/answer.md (Elias), girl/girl_in.md + girl/answer.md (Maren), day1.md + day2.md (prior canon). All dialogue below is quoted verbatim from the answer files. Day 2's open threads — the number, Callum's reply, Pat's reaction, the Dad conversation — are all addressed; nothing reset.*
4|
5|---
6|
7|## Scene 1 — 6:55am, Ferndale Road, one bed and one kitchen
8|
9|The board is triple-stacked — two no-heats carried over from Friday plus the landlord round — and the radio has upgraded the frost: hard from midnight, Sunday morning guaranteed to kill boilers across town [boy/boy_in.md]. Mare traded the double-time away for this weekend, so the quiet is the first gift of the day. He lets her sleep. Thermos filled, kiss on the hair, gone by seven [boy/answer.md].
10|
11|Her side of the same minute: a kiss that didn't check its watch [girl/girl_in.md]. She wakes to an empty house that smells of nothing burnt, no shift, daylight — and two things already waiting on her phone.
12|
13|## Scene 2 — 8:15–8:50am, her kitchen: two messages, two answers
14|
15|Pat, 8:15: roast at one, bring that bread from the Polish shop, "the ladies will sit at one and the men can come when the men are ready," Callum coming "which will be lovely" [girl/girl_in.md]. So Elias kept his word — he told her — and it changed nothing Pat says out loud. The ward, 8:35: short-handed, clinic only, any chance of four hours. The world keeps offering money for exactly the thing she said she wasn't selling.
16|
17|At 8:50 she answers the ward [girl/answer.md]:
18|
19|> "Can't today. Ring me for a Tuesday evening if clinic runs late."
20|
21|Not never — just not the thing she said she wasn't selling. Then the Polish shop, Pat's bread bought *because she chooses to*, and two texts while the queue crawls [girl/answer.md]:
22|
23|> "Heard from your mum. Roast at one, bread sorted. One thing before Sunday: I'm not doing 'the ladies sit at one.' We arrive together or I sit where the chairs land."
24|
25|> "Thank you for telling her. That counted."
26|
27|A boundary and a kept-word credit, issued in the same breath. She is learning to do both at once.
28|
29|## Scene 3 — 9:10am, Van 2, between jobs: the scale
30|
31|He rings her before the second job, because the number is thirty-six hours old and the order fires Monday [boy/answer.md]:
32|
33|> "Morning. Three numbers, and none of them is mine yet. Fifty — feeds the fund slow, gone by spring. Hundred-fifty — steady, rebuilt by summer. Two-fifty — same as before, which broke once. You slide the scale, I'll sign wherever your finger lands. Today, though. It fires Monday."
34|
35|Then he lays Callum's non-answer on the table too — the 10:40pm *xmas is tight mate ill see what i can do*, no amount, no date, silence with extra steps [boy/boy_in.md] — and hands her the verdict before he hands himself one:
36|
37|> "He said 'I'll see,' which is a no wearing a maybe's coat. I want to let it lie till after Sunday. Tell me if you'd say something sooner — your read counts as much as mine."
38|
39|Her read is not recorded on the page [girl/answer.md is silent on Callum]. The hold — let it lie till after Sunday — stands as proposed, unopposed. Two solo decisions was the old life; there is no third strike coming [boy/answer.md].
40|
41|## Scene 4 — Dusk, the vans serviced
42|
43|His day eats the board job by job; the frost waits at midnight like a booked customer [boy/boy_in.md]. Her day is bread by the door, car keys beside it, and a line loaded for tomorrow's table, rehearsed in a light voice, knife in butter [girl/answer.md]:
44|
45|> "We're all ready, Pat. Some of us just get asked later."
46|
47|Deniable English has met its translator. The line waits for Sunday.
48|
49|## Scene 5 — Evening, kettle on: the number
50|
51|She opens it herself. Sentences like *pick a number with me* don't get to just sit [girl/answer.md]:
52|
53|> "Mine's £150 a month, reviewed whenever one of us says review. Say yours out loud, even if it's different. Especially if it's different. Monday doesn't get to fire something we never said."
54|
55|His out-loud was already on record — the 9:10 pledge: *I'll sign wherever your finger lands* [boy/answer.md]. Her finger lands on the middle number. His scale, her voice, one figure: **£150 a month, review on demand, fires Monday signed.** The Ferndale Fund's first jointly-set terms in its existence — *steady, rebuilt by summer*, his own words come back as her choice [bible §Tension 1; day2.md Decision 6].
56|
57|## Scene 6 — Later that night: the last untold thing
58|
59|Vans serviced, home late, he says it before it can ambush him at Tom's table [boy/answer.md]:
60|
61|> "Tomorrow will be loud in me. The frost, the vans humming — it'll sound like him dispatching. If I go quiet at the table, it's not the food and it's not Callum. Just... reach over and touch my arm, yeah?"
62|
63|By his own count, that was the last untold thing. Told not as confession but as request — the ask-first idiom, learned in four days. The deeper terror underneath it, being Tom, still hasn't been said in those words [bible §Never-Says]; what he said tonight is its shape. She has her instruction for tomorrow, and it costs her nothing but the reach of an arm.
64|
65|## Scene 7 — How the day ended
66|
67|The kettle cools on the hob. In the notebook, under page one, the newest entry is still his actual words; tonight adds no new page because today's truest lines were spoken, not written [bible §Quirks; girl/answer.md]. At midnight the frost arrives on schedule, and every boiler in town starts dying for Sunday's richest morning of the year [boy/boy_in.md]. Lights out on Ferndale Road with one o'clock waiting, Pat's table set, and a man's grief pre-translated for the woman sitting next to him.
68|
